name: ro-array-core-power-split
description: Issue #811: the shipped array (ro_ring11 x2, ro_buf x2, xor2 x1, design/ro_array_core.spice) with its single vdd rail split into three zero-volt-metered rails, one per ro_buf and one for the xor2, so the 'ring buffers + XOR' remainder of ro-array-core-pvt-q can be attributed. Same rails, kick, tran 5p 300n window and edge pairing as ro-array-core-pvt-q. Run at ff / -40 C / 3.63 V only. Measurement only; no design change.
tstep: 5p (print step; it also caps ngspice's own solver step, as in ro-array-core-pvt-q)
analyses: tran 5p 300n
meas tran t1a when v(ro1)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran t1b when v(ro1)=v(vth) rise=6
meas tran t2a when v(ro2)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran t2b when v(ro2)=v(vth) rise=6
meas tran c1a find v(q1) when v(ro1)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran c1b find v(q1) when v(ro1)=v(vth) rise=6
meas tran c2a find v(q2) when v(ro2)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran c2b find v(q2) when v(ro2)=v(vth) rise=6
meas tran cb1a find v(qb1) when v(ro1)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran cb1b find v(qb1) when v(ro1)=v(vth) rise=6
meas tran cb2a find v(qb2) when v(ro2)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran cb2b find v(qb2) when v(ro2)=v(vth) rise=6
meas tran cxa find v(qx) when v(ro1)=v(vth) rise=2
meas tran cxb find v(qx) when v(ro1)=v(vth) rise=6
meas tran vhi max v(ro1) from=200n to=295n
meas tran vlo min v(ro1) from=200n to=295n
meas tran vxhi max v(xo) from=200n to=295n
meas tran vxlo min v(xo) from=200n to=295n
let cq = 1e-9
let nper = 4
caveats: Single corner (ff / -40 C / 3.63 V), the corner at which the array term of the whole-block active power binds. Says nothing about any other corner.

The deck instantiates ro_ring11, ro_buf and xor2 directly because ro_array_core has one vdd pin; sim/tests/test_active_power_breakdown.py pins the instance set and connectivity to design/ro_array_core.spice. The only electrical difference from the shipped array is the metering split of vdd into vddb1, vddb2 and vddx, all zero-impedance taps off the same ideal vsup.

Reconciliation target: sim/records/2026-08-02-ro-array-core-pvt-q-39.md (same corner), whose p_total_w - p_rings_w is 120.033 uW. This deck's p_tree_w (buffers + XOR) is 121.950 uW, +1.60 % from it, inside the 2 % tolerance sim/tools/active_power_breakdown.py enforces. The residual is not attributed: the two records were minted on different hosts and PDK checkouts, and the rings agree to 0.0004 % (273.125 vs 273.125 uW), so it sits in the tree branch.

p_bufs_w + p_xor_w (= p_tree_w) is the whole power of the buffers and the XOR, not a recoverable amount: they must still drive the sampler. It is an upper bound on what any trim in that row could return.
The XOR current depends on input activity; its inputs here are the free-running rings' buffered outputs, as in ro-array-core-pvt-q.
Deterministic (mismatch-free, noiseless) transient: one nominal device draw. Neither mismatch nor jitter is measured.
